front.title: How are you doing?
front.lede: 20 taps, about a minute. Then you see what lifts you and what weighs on you.
how.title: How it works
how.kept: What is kept: your 20 taps, your role, the day, the language and the random code. In a room, also the room and the round, as a code no one can trace back. Your age and country only if you tap them. Nothing else.
how.no_name: No name, no email, no address, no IP address. A random code on this phone is all that links your answers.
how.count: Every check-in adds to an anonymous count for the day and the country: numbers only, with no code, so it cannot lead back to you. That count draws the curves.
how.wait: Your answers wait on the server for your yes. A no deletes them at once. No answer: they are deleted after 24 hours.
how.room: In a room, your taps are added to the room's totals. The host sees totals only, from 10 phones, never a person.
how.study: Your answers go into a study of what helps people feel well, and what weighs on them, in different groups and countries. Results are published only as groups, never as one person.
how.join: If you also said yes in Find out who you are, the two can be studied together through the same random code. Nothing else joins them.
how.delete: Delete any time: {link}. Data already published cannot be pulled back.
how.forget_sure: This removes your check-in answers, right now.
how.forgotten: Done. Nothing of yours is kept.
how.yes_count: {n} people have said yes so far.
foot.research: Every question, its source and how the result is worked out:
item.role.help: If you both study and work, tap the one that fills more of your week.
help.who: Please indicate for each of the five statements which is closest to how you have been feeling over the last two weeks. Notice that higher numbers mean better well-being.
item.w1: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits
item.w2: I have felt calm and relaxed
item.w3: I have felt active and vigorous
item.w4: I woke up feeling fresh and rested
item.w5: My daily life has been filled with things that interest me
who.opt.3: More than half of the time
who.opt.2: Less than half of the time
item.st.lead: Stress means a situation in which a person feels tense, restless, nervous or anxious or is unable to sleep at night because his/her mind is troubled all the time.
item.st: Do you feel this kind of stress these days?
item.y_load.work: Do you get behind with your work?
item.y_load.study: Do you get behind with your studies?
item.y_load.other: Do you get behind with the things you have to do?
item.y_control.work: Do you have any influence on HOW you do your work?
item.y_control.study: Do you have any influence on HOW you study?
item.y_control.other: Do you have any influence on HOW you do the things you have to do?
item.y_support.work: How often do you get help and support from your colleagues, if needed?
item.y_support.study: How often do you get help and support from other students, if needed?
item.y_support.other: How often do you get help and support from the people around you, if needed?
item.y_recog.work: Is your work recognized and appreciated by the management?
item.y_recog.study: Is your work recognized and appreciated by your teachers?
item.y_recog.other: Is what you do recognized and appreciated by the people around you?
item.y_future.work: Are you worried about becoming unemployed?
item.y_future.study: Are you worried about failing your studies?
item.y_future.other: Are you worried about your future?
item.mind: The biggest thing on my mind this week
mind.country: What's going on in the country
item.p_say: People like me have a say in what happens around us.
item.p_deserve: Compared with others, I get what I deserve.
item.p_better: Life for people like me is getting better.
item.p_leftout: How often do you feel left out?
item.ladder: Think of this ladder as representing where people stand {in_country}. At the top of the ladder are the people who are the best off – those who have the most money, the most education, and the most respected jobs. At the bottom are the people who are the worst off – those who have the least money, least education, the least respected jobs, or no job. The higher up you are on this ladder, the closer you are to the people at the very top; the lower you are, the closer you are to the people at the very bottom. Where would you place yourself on this ladder?
res.title: Your check-in
res.scale: Your last two weeks, from 0 to 100
res.bandline.1: Some weeks are like this. It's worth talking to someone you trust.
res.bandline.2: More good days than hard ones. Below: what lifts you, and what weighs on you.
res.bandline.3: A good two weeks. Below: what lifts you.
res.kind: These two weeks have been hard. You don't have to carry this alone.
res.talk: Talk to someone you trust: a friend, family, a doctor.
res.talk_student: Talk to someone you trust: a friend, family, a teacher, a doctor.
res.danger: In danger right now? Call your local emergency number.
res.come_back: Come back in two weeks and see what moved.
res.room: See how your class or team is doing →
advice.y_load: Too much to do? Go for a ten-minute walk anyway. It helps more than it sounds.
advice.y_control: Pick one thing you want to learn this week, just for you.
advice.y_support: Talk to one person today. Family, a friend, anyone.
advice.y_recog: Thank someone this week for something they did.
advice.y_meaning: Help someone with something small this week.
advice.y_future: Worried about what's coming? Stop for a minute and look at what's around you right now.
advice.sleep: Teenagers need 8 to 10 hours, adults 7 to 9. Try to go to bed and get up at about the same time every day.
advice.p_say: Join something near you: a club, a team, a group that does things together.
advice.p_deserve: Tonight, think of one good thing that happened today.
advice.p_better: Give yourself one small goal for this week, one you'll be glad to reach.
advice.p_leftout: Say yes to one plan with other people this week. Or make one.
advice.none: You're doing the things that keep people well. Keep going.
consent.text: I'm Khayyam, a scientist, the kind who studies politics. May I keep your answers for research? You stay anonymous.
consent.thanks: Thank you. Your answers are in.
consent.declined: Done. Nothing of yours is kept.

host.lede: Everyone answers on their own phone, in about a minute. You see the group, never a person.

host.lever.y_load: Ask for less this week, and say what matters most.
host.lever.y_control: Let people decide how they do a task, or in what order.
host.lever.y_support: Give people time to help each other. Pairs, a short talk at the start, an open door.
host.lever.y_recog: When someone does good work, tell them. Soon, and to their face.
host.lever.y_meaning: Tell people what each task is for and who it helps.
host.lever.y_future: Tell people early what's coming, why, and when. Even if it's not all decided yet.
host.ask_first: Ask your group first. They usually know what would help.
